contract: The no-C-compiler job is expected to FAIL while this list is non-empty, and expected to fail ONLY for reasons on it. A failure whose reason is absent here is a regression, not progress. The list is the phase's schedule: it shrinks patch by patch, and the job becomes required when it empties -- by a patch that says so, never automatically.

entries.reason: build/gust-runtime-package.a carries glibc-only undefined symbols, so it cannot link against musl and the C-free link cannot be proved.
entries.cleared_by: NOT 25.5/25.6, and not by removing C at all -- Patch 25.10a removed the last C from this archive and the entry survived. Clearing it needs a musl Rust target (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl), because the remaining symbols come from Rust's std.

patch2510a_measurement.why: they came from C compiled with -O2 -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE, and there is no C in the archive now
patch2510a_measurement.not_verified_by_linking: no musl toolchain on the measuring host; this is a symbol census, not a link attempt

entries.reason: src/runtime/*.c is 1,968 hand-written lines compiled by $(CC); every binary links it.
entries.cleared_by: 25.5, 25.6 and 25.10a for src/runtime/*.c; the last 29 lines are 25.10's, because src/runtime.c exists only to be cat-ed into emitted C

patch2510a_measurement.remaining: src/runtime.c, 29 lines, not compiled by $(CC) into the runtime -- it is the unity #include header for the emitted-C route

entries.reason: rustc uses cc as its linker driver on *-linux-gnu, including for the musl self-contained target, so a C-free link needs -C linker=rust-lld explicitly.
entries.cleared_by: 25.11 -- cc optional, musl + rust-lld proved here

entries.reason: The Cranelift backend links its objects by spawning a C driver: compiler/experiments/cranelift/src/main.rs:16533 reads `env::var_os("CC").unwrap_or_else(|| "cc")`. Removing C COMPILATION from the tree does not remove C LINKING from the native route.
entries.measured_by: Patch 25.10, by running the workload after the bootstrap chain was deleted
entries.cleared_by: an internal or non-cc link step for the native backend -- lld, or a linker invoked directly rather than through a C driver. Not by any further C deletion, because there is no C left to delete on this path.
entries.observable_note: Newly observable. It was always true and never the thing that failed, because the Makefile died at its first $(CC) line before the native route was reached. Patch 25.10 deleted that chain, so this became the failure rather than becoming a fact.

excepted.reason: Editor tooling. Makefile:262 test target never names test_tree_sitter, no workflow mentions it, and the only routes are explicit opt-in. Optional under D10, so out of scope rather than on the schedule.
